key_insight: A subdomain-wise conditional diffusion model can reconstruct full hypersonic boundary-layer fields from limited top-wall data while preserving multiscale structure and uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This offers a probabilistic surrogate for near-wall hypersonic turbulence where direct measurements are sparse, enabling better state estimation and wall-quantity prediction.
method: Split the wall-normal boundary layer into overlapping subdomains and reconstruct each with a single Mach- and height-conditioned EDM.
Use soft overlap inpainting to stitch subdomain samples into a continuous full-field volume.
Add a bounded binned spectral power loss to retain high-wavenumber content without instability during diffusion training.
evidence_signal: The model was validated on DNS data for Mach 6, 7, and 8, recovering instantaneous structures, spectra, statistics, correlations, wall quantities, and uncertainty patterns.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on the quality of top-wall conditioning and careful tuning of overlap/inpainting and spectral-loss settings for stable deployment.
paper_title: Multiscale Hypersonic Boundary Layer Reconstruction via Spectral Binning and Subdomain-wise Conditional Diffusion
